requirement: A lessee must submit the results of its site characterization surveys to BOEM with its Site Assessment Plan (SAP), Construction and Operations Plan (COP), or General Activities Plan (GAP).
scope: Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf, Site Assessment Plan, Construction and Operations Plan, General Activities Plan
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic habitat survey; site characterization

requirement: The information will be used by BOEM, other Federal agencies, and potentially affected states in the preparation of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) documents.
A plan (SAP, COP, or GAP) must describe biological, social, and economic resource information potentially affected by activities proposed in the SAP, COP, or GAP.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; biological resources; social resources; economic resources

requirement: The lessee should prepare a benthic habitat survey plan that describes its methods for collecting sufficient information on the biology and seafloor morphology of the survey area.
scope: Survey area for wind energy turbines on the Atlantic OCS
related_domains: benthic habitat assessment; marine biology; seafloor morphology

requirement: BOEM may determine that it is prudent for a developer to resurvey some or all of the lease area in the event survey results are insufficient.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic habitat survey

requirement: The applicant should employ the appropriate equipment and analytical techniques for all surveys.
The applicant should identify the reasonably foreseeable effects associated with their proposed activity and ensure that the habitats that could be affected are included in their surveys.
scope: All phases of the proposed action
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic habitat protection

requirement: BOEM recommends applicants submit survey specifications with a SAP, COP, or GAP survey plan.
scope: Survey specifications for SAP, COP, or GAP

requirement: The survey specifications should state the issues to be investigated, hypotheses, assumptions, data collection techniques, standards, analytical and statistical techniques, and quality control.
scope: Survey specifications for SAP, COP, or GAP
related_domains: survey methodology; data collection; quality control

requirement: Conduct 2 years of seasonal surveys (spring, summer, fall, winter).
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic community monitoring

requirement: Baseline survey should include an appropriate sample size from the entire area of potential adverse effect, generally not less than one sample per 1-2 km along a proposed line of potential adverse effect or one sample per 1-2 km2 within a proposed area of potential adverse effect.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic community monitoring

requirement: Special attention should be given to the presence of sensitive benthic habitats.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; benthic habitat protection

requirement: Side scan sonar data should be of optimal quality resulting in the displays automatically corrected for slant range, lay-back and vessel speed.
Mosaic the recorded data to provide a true plan view that provides 100 percent coverage of the area of potential adverse effect.
Tow the sonar instrument above the seafloor at a distance that is 10 to 20 percent of the range of the instrument.

Ensure line spacing and display range are appropriate for the water depth and data obtained are of such quality as to permit detection and evaluation of seafloor objects and features 0.5m – 1m in diameter within the survey area.
Completion of any necessary permit requirements (e.g. Marine Mammal Protection Act if harassment of marine mammals may occur from the activity).
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine life protection

requirement: Identify and confirm which benthic species (flora and fauna) inhabit the proposed project development site.
NMFS-designated essential fish habitat (EFH) for eggs, larvae, juveniles, adults, and spawning adults must be identified within the action area.
Characterize benthic community composition including documentation of abundance, diversity, percent cover, and community structure.
Characterize and delineate the surficial sediment layers in the area.
Characterize the physical hydrodynamic properties of the surrounding water column.
Characterize both manmade and natural physical bottom disturbance typical for the action area.
Identify area(s) of similar physical and biological characteristics outside the action area which may be used as a baseline reference.
